5	Polyply is a Python suite for generating input files and system coordinates for

13	  *Nature Communications* 13, 68 (2022),
14	  DOI: `10.1038/s41467-021-27627-4`.
15	
16	The README and docs explain that Polyply can:
17	
18	- generate input files for polymer and biomacromolecule simulations;
19	- use user-specified building blocks or library polymers;
20	- generate coordinates with a multiscale random-walk workflow;
21	- tailor initial chain conformations through build files.
22	
23	## Build-file reference context
24	
25	The build-file syntax reference says that build files can supply:
26	
27	- user-defined residue records;
28	- residue volumes as LJ sigma values in nm;
29	- additional geometric and distance restraints for structure generation.
30	
31	The writing-ff-input-files guide explains how residue definitions and links are
32	used to build polymer input files, and the quick-start guide shows the
33	coordinate-generation workflow that consumes those inputs.
34	
35	## Why this context matters
36	
37	The public fixture and reproduction exercise the normal coordinate-generation
38	workflow for a small polymer system. The public documentation is enough to
39	understand the intended scientific behavior of the workflow.

## Root cause

The supplied build file (`test.bld`) defines a `[template]` section, so the build-file parser attaches user templates (keyed by resname) to every molecule. `GenerateTemplates.run_molecule` converts those into placeholder entries `{resname: None}` and hands them to `group_residues_by_hash` — which tried to run the Weisfeiler-Lehman graph hash on the `None` placeholder and crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'is_multigraph'` before any coordinates were produced.

A second, same-family defect: `_extract_template_graphs`'s `skip_filter=True` branch computed the residue-graph hashes but never annotated meta-molecule nodes with the `"template"` hash, while `Backmap` and `NonBondEngine` unconditionally read that annotation — so every valid `-skip_filter` run died downstream with a `KeyError`.

## Fix (two minimal, design-consistent edits)

- `source/polyply/src/check_residue_equivalence.py:68-71` — `group_residues_by_hash` now skips `None` placeholders (non-graph entries can't be hashed); real template graphs are hashed as before, docstring updated.
- `source/polyply/src/generate_templates.py:44` — the `skip_filter` branch now sets `meta_molecule.nodes[node]["template"] = graph_hash`, matching the documented annotation contract of the non-skip branch (`group_residues_by_hash`).

No fixture-specific values are hard-coded; the full scientific pipeline (template optimization, volume estimation, random walk, backmapping) runs unchanged.
